title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for diabetes and kidney function.

HPI
The patient is a 62-year-old male presenting for a scheduled follow-up regarding his type 2 diabetes and renal status. He reports adherence to his current regimen and denies any acute concerns or new symptoms. He has been managed on long-term insulin therapy and does not take any other medications for his glucose levels. He notes that his kidney function has remained stable over the last three months.

Medication List
- Insulin (long-term)

Exam
The patient appears well-nourished and in no acute distress. Vital signs are stable. Skin is intact without lesions. Heart sounds are regular. Lungs are clear to auscultation.

Assessment
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus: Stable on current insulin therapy.
2. Chronic kidney disease stage 4: The patient's renal decline is not related to diabetes.

Plan
1. Continue current insulin dosage as prescribed.
2. Monitor renal function labs every three months.
3. Follow up in the clinic in 12 weeks.
explanations: The provider states the CKD is not due to diabetes, so the presumed link does not apply: code diabetes without complications and CKD separately.
Code also the CKD stage (N18.4) as instructed at the diabetes CKD code or separately when unrelated.
Long-term insulin use in type 2 diabetes: add Z79.4.

distractors.why: The 'with' presumption is overridden when the provider documents another cause or no link.
The stage of CKD must be reported with N18.-.
Z79.4 is required for routine insulin use in type 2 diabetes.
